utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, would you like to call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Hase Icic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a blank screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have the same situation here as well. MR. HASE ICIC, called

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Sir, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Hase Icic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what year were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: November 3rd 1948.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you born, Mr. Icic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Hrnici on the border of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosniak Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you grow up in the area of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you attend school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One part in Trnopolje and the rest of the primary school in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At the Rade Kondic school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Icic, did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: End of '67 and I also served through 69, that is the 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After your military service, did you become involved in work in Germany in approximately 1970 as a construction worker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that your occupation until shortly before the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you still consider Trnopolje, Trnopolje area, your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you build a house in the Trnopolje area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the years you spent in Germany how often would you return home to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every 15 days, sometimes even every week, over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long would you stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes just over the weekend, and often times the whole week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you did return home did you stay inside the house or did you tend to go out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at home the least, because I needed to find supplies in Kozarac, and friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you did see your friends or go for supplies, where would you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Icic, do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since the school days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know the members of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you go to school with any members of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with Mladen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you play together with Mladin as children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we played soccer in the soccer field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you grew up and before you became involved with your work in Germany, did you continue to see Dule Tadic in Kozarac regularly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we would meet, we would pass each other with the company that Dule Tadic kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During your regular visits home during the time you were in Germany or working in Germany, when you went to Kozarac for supplies or to cafes did you also continue to see Dule Tadic regularly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would you sometimes be in the same cafes together sitting a few feet apart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the years you knew him, did you see him sometimes with a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see him sometimes without a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you familiar with his appearance both with and without a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Icic, in late April 1992 did you return home to visit Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On that visit were you able to return to Germany to resume work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, all bridges towards Croatia were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you in the Trnopolje area when the attack on Kozarac began on May 24th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could you hear the shelling of the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did people from the area of Kozarac flee toward Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that a few people or a large number of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A large number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the attack on Kozarac began, was there an announcement that the people of the area of Trnopolje should surrender weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were weapons collected and turned over to Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As far as you are aware, were all the weapons that people in the area of Trnopolje possessed turned over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see what was collected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was very little, several M48 rifles which belonged to the TO members, and some hunting arms and then, you know, there were these rifles that you shoot birds with.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Are those air rifles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain in the area of Trnopolje until June 14th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On that day did Serbian forces come to the area of Trnopolje to collect Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you see on that day? Who came in? How many Serb forces, what kinds of vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see all of the Serb forces, but I saw a tank that was sitting in front of my house, and the soldiers who ordered that men be separated from women, also boys older than 16. They took them to a truck that was behind the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you taken on that truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then were you taken to a collection point in the area of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken in front of the house of Hamid Sivac in Sivci.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From there were you and other men placed on buses and taken away from the Trnopolje area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you held in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what part of Keraterm were you held, Mr. Icic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In room No. 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately until 7th or 8th June.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were the general conditions in Keraterm like during the period of time you were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bad, very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you describe the conditions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know, there was nothing to lie on, except the concrete. A few people had palettes that remained from the warehouse and then the toilets were all plugged up and it all stank. There was no water to wash and there was almost no food, and when the food arrived it was not enough for everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: There seems to be some confusion of dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Miss Sutherland was just pointing that out, your Honour. Thank you. Mr. Icic, may I ask you again, until approximately what date did you remain in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Keraterm I stayed until 7th or 8th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners regularly called from the rooms in which they were held and beaten or tortured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners regularly called from their rooms and killed or disappeared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, both.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Icic, were you interrogated while in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kinds of questions were you asked during your interrogation there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know, almost none. They started with my explaining to them what my heritage, my forefathers and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they take a statement from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point during the interrogation did they ask you about weapons or politics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About the weapons at the very end, whether I had any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On approximately 7th or 8th July where were you transferred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately how many other prisoners from Keraterm were transferred with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A whole bus, approximately 40 to 50 detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the nationality of those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were some of them members of the Reserve Police, as far as you were aware?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time did you arrive in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 7th or 8th July, I do not remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time of the day was that, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around noon, around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were guards or soldiers or other Serb forces waiting for you when the bus arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did the bus stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the bus came to a stop they were already, one could say, prepared, welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what part of the camp was it that the bus stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between the dining room and that large red building with the door towards the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Using that pointer which is located to the right of the console, can you show us the approximate position where the bus stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model] Approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the bus stopped how were the guards or soldiers positioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They lined up like, sort of, a cordon, and the prisoners had to go through it. I had to go through it, between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did that cordon run from, from the bus to where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the entrance to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were the prisoners called off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One by one, easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened as you and the other prisoners got off the bus and went toward the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the moment when I was called out, I had to get off the bus and to start walking towards the white house. I went between the guards who were in civilian clothes or police uniforms who were holding different objects and they were hitting from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you got to the white house where were you placed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was placed in the last room on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Other than the prisoners you had arrived with, were there other prisoners in that room when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not there had been prisoners in that room before your arrival or where those prisoners went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you and the others were put in that room, were you again called out from that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you sent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had to go to interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were you called out when you were sent to interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same way pretty much as when we were getting off the bus, one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there also a cordon, that is, two rows of guards leading from the white house toward the area where you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was the same cordon, but not as many, some had left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you go alone or were you escorted by a guard when you went to interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to go with a guard who walked in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened as you went through the cordon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They hit me again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you make any effort to run or walk faster to avoid the blows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not because he would not let me go any faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the room above the restaurant, the last one to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What questions were you asked when you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had in front of him a statement from Keraterm and he read it out to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he ask you anything about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me whether I had anything to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I had nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the interrogation was over, where were you sent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was returned to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you go by yourself or were you again escorted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Escorted by another guard who was next to the interrogator the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you again beaten as you went from the interrogation back to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this one did not allow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you returned to the white house, did you return to the same room you had been in before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was returned to the last room on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you returned from interrogation, Mr. Icic, at some point did Serbs enter your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you and the others in your room ordered to do anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were you ordered to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To lie down on our stomach, with our arms stretched over our heads and with three fingers together because that is how the Serbs pray.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there enough space for all of you to lie stretched out in this fashion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, not enough for all of us to stretch out, but we had to make enough room so that our hands are free and so that those three fingers can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you and the others had taken this position, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then Serbs entered, walked over us, jumped, looked to see if the fingers were in the proper position, if not, they would strike them with a rifle butt and shouted with happiness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they shouting anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Be a great Serb, you Serb".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did any of the Serbs who came in have knives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they using those knives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They cut, they slashed the clothes on our backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were some of the prisoners cut as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you cut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not cut, but they slashed my leather jacket and the sweater under it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the leather jacket protected you from actually having your body cut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When one of the Serbs who came in cut your jacket, did another one react to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he felt sorry for the jacket because he had been waiting for such a jacket for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to the person who had cut up the jacket?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He swore at him but he, nevertheless, took the jacket although it was cut.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they cutting the clothes and the prisoners in any particular way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were making crosses on our backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After those persons left the room, were you and the others let alone for a period of time that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Later on did someone come into the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Krkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know at that time who Krkan was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had you heard about Krkan from anyone in the white house that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you learn about Krkan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time before anybody tortured us, a girl called Hajra Hodzic entered the room and next to me was sitting a friend who knew her, and she told him a story and also told him to beware of Krkan because he was the one who called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you later find out what Krkan's position in the camp was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the head of the guard shift or the Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Krkan bring anything with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He brought a clean sheet of paper and a pencil.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he instruct the prisoners what they were to do with that paper and pencil?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he told us that each one of us was to sign his name on a sheet of paper, and to turn over all the belongings he had on him, that is, money, foreign exchange, jewellery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he indicate whether or not what benefits prisoners might receive from contributing their valuables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said if the amount would be enough, we would be spared any further torture.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was each prisoner somehow to indicate how much he had individually contributed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were you supposed to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Each one of us was to put down all that he had turned over and the amount of money next to his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then did Krkan leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He left immediately after telling us what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Later on did he return?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had the prisoners put their names on the piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we all signed our names and I signed my name and surname. I signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there any valuables or gold or jewellery on the table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why had not the prisoners in your room surrendered any valuables or gold?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because all that had been taken away in Keraterm already.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So there were no valuables on the table and there was a list of prisoners names with nothing written next to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing, apart from the names of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Krkan say anything when he saw there were no valuables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he take the list with him and leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he took the list and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Later on, Mr. Icic, did a group come to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it still daylight or was it already dark by that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you become aware that a group was coming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could hear it from the adjacent room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they in the adjacent room or were prisoners saying that a group was coming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could hear from the adjacent room how they were saying, "Here, the executioners are coming".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When this group came into the white house, what did they first start to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were carrying something with them. They brought some implements and set up lighting in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there a light in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As the members of the group were in the process of doing that, were you able to see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we could watch them at leisure, I could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it normally dangerous in camp or risky to look at guards or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not dangerous until they would order you not to look. Until such time one could look, one could watch, as long as one wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there an order not to look on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Krkan come back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to the prisoners in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While they were putting up that lighting he did not say anything. They only talked among themselves, the group that had arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to see how many members of that group there were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were five of them and Krkan was the sixth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those five persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of them as people you had known before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who did you recognise because you knew them before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Dule Tadic, Simo Kevic, because them I knew before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you recognised Dule Tadic and Simo Kevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of them as people you had known or seen in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the two of them I knew from before the war and others -- the other two I recognised because they used to come to Keraterm daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who did you recognise as people you knew from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Banovic and one called Duca, he was in Keraterm day after day after day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You said there were five people, did you recognise the fifth person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the fifth one I did see but I learned his surname while they were talking amongst themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What surname did you hear used for this person while they were talking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they called him "Babic".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After some sort of improvised lighting system was set up, did someone say they would be calling prisoners out of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Krkan came to the door and told us that now he would start calling out and every person called out was to come out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he begin calling prisoners out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the prisoners called out in any particular order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In sequence down the list that we had made ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When a prisoner was called and left the room, could you see in which direction he went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was taken to a room on the left, a small room at the end of the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After each prisoner was called out and went toward the small room at the end of the corridor, could you hear what was happening in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We heard blows.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could you hear the sounds of prisoners crying in pain or screaming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know what was happening in there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, all we heard were blows.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After each prisoner was called out and you heard the sounds of blows coming from that small room at the end of the corridor, did you see the prisoners again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them every time when a prisoner would be beaten up because they would throw him out into another room, the first one that we had been to when we got off the buses, the room -- across the room in which I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After a period of time did the group that had come to the white house and was calling prisoners out take some kind of break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About how many prisoners had been called into that small room by that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 10 and 15 prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did the group go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went to the area in front of the white house, out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know what they were doing out there? Could you hear what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard them. They were drinking, holding toasts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In addition to drinking or at least to making toasts, were they discussing anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were discussing the further roles, what would each one of them do next.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Icic, you indicated that you heard the name of Babic used during discussions between members of this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the period of time they were setting up the light or when they were outside talking, did you hear any other names used by members of this group to other members of the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they used their proper names, the whole group.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What names do you recall hearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do remember, they were simply talking. They were outside. We were very quiet, there was not a sound inside, and we listened to their conversation and we heard that this was going to do this, "Babic will do that because he is a specialist in that", and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What names do you recall? What names were used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Dule" they used, "Babic", "Simo". They used all the names that I had already mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After being outside, did the group return back to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they resume calling prisoners out from your room again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the time come when your name was called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you do when your name was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came to the door and looked to the right. It was the exit from the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why did you look to the right if all the prisoners had been going left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I turned left but I looked right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you see when you looked right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I saw two guards at the entrance to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you paused and looked right, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Krkan pulled me to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Toward the small room at the back of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you stepped toward or into the doorway of that small room, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I faced a group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you were moving into the room ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I entered the room in front of me directly face to face was Dule Tadic standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there anyone near him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simo Kevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you entered the room were you ordered to do anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to greet them Serb way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was it you were told to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to say, "God be with you, heros".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you did that what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, one of them immediately put a noose around my neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, one of them put a -- our translation here is not completely clear. What was it that was put around your neck, Mr. Icic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A noose around the neck. You know what it looks like?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that noose was put around your neck, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He pulled it tight and I was pulled, and at the same moment one of them dealt me such a heavy blow on my back that I fell on my stomach.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you fell on your stomach what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then they went on beating me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were they beating you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All sorts of things, with those implements they had with them as they were setting up the lighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kind of implements were those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they had a whip made of a cable which ended in iron balls, they had an iron rod, they had a wooden bat and some rubber sticks special for the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How tight was the noose around your neck during this time? Were you struggling to breathe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no air.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to scream?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point was the noose loosened a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when they would loosen it a little bit they would beat more because they could see I was alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point during this process did you lose consciousness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you regain your consciousness that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, several times, but only briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the morning did you recover your consciousness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning I was a little bit more conscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was lying among other battered people in that room in which I was when I had got off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was happening when you regained consciousness in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was then that one of the guards entered, walked over us, and looked to see how many were dead among us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the guard walk on you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he put his foot on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened when he did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I let a cry of pain to which he responded, "He's alive but not for long".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened to those prisoners who were determined to be dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They carried them out. They took them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who carried them out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Prisoners who were not from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Icic, that evening or the evening following, did you again hear the sounds of beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were those sounds coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were coming from outside, from in front of the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was a man by the name of Hrvat called from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he ever return to the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you continue to hear the sounds of beating after he was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could go on hearing the sounds of beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what position were you in the room at this time? Were you standing or lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not stand up. I was on the floor on my back. That was the only position I could be in. My head and my shoulders were partly on another body.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what direction were you facing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the direction of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How far from the door were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not far from the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you were lying on your back with your head and shoulders off the ground against another prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there any lighting in the hallway at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that moment when I was looking out to the hallway only the hallway was lit with some source of light from the outside, or maybe there were some improvised light, in other words, only the hallway was lit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point did you hear the sounds of people approaching the doorway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard as people were approaching and cursing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you heard that cursing, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw as they drag a beaten up person.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did they do with that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They sort of threw it in the room at my feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many people dragged that beaten up person into your room or to the room and threw him in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise either of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After Dule Tadic and the other man threw the beaten up man into the room, did either of them say anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Dule Tadic said, "You will remember, Sivac, that you cannot touch a Serb or say anything to a Serb".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At that point did you know who he was referring to when he used the name "Sivac"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment I was not sure who he was referring to, because there are several people named "Sivac".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the person who had been thrown into the room say anything or ask for anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he asked for water.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did someone try to give him some water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he able to drink it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the morning were you able to see who that person who had been thrown into the room was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when it became light.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My old friend and cousin, Sefik Sivac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On that morning did anyone come to see the condition of the prisoners or who was dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Krkan came.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did he want to know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He wanted to find out the names of the people who were either dead or who could not move.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you tell him who Sefik Sivac was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that this was Sefik Sivac, the owner of the cafes, BMW and De Luxe, in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was the BMW cafe located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor, at the marketplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Later on did other prisoners speak to you about saying this to Krkan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the other prisoners told me that I was crazy because I told him that. I did not care. I was just waiting to be finished off.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had Sefik Sivac been in your room before he was thrown into your room by Dule Tadic and the other man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know where he had been before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Dule Tadic and Sefik Sivac know each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had they been friends at one time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they on good terms before the war began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because Sefik threw him out of his cafe Luxe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That morning was Sefik Sivac removed from the room along with other dead prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right away. He was carried out together with the other ones who were either dead or unconscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Icic, on the two nights you saw Dule Tadic in the white house do you recall what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not he had a beard or was clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Long or short?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not too long, short-ish.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: A couple of days after Mr. Sivac was taken from the white house, were you and other prisoners taken from the white house and put outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken in front of the white house so that they could clean up the stench -- you could not just endure it any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the guards took you out of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not me. I was taken out by my fellow inmates who had not been beaten yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: They assisted you out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The reason you were taken out of the white house was because the guards could not stand the stench any more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you sit once you were taken out of the white house on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of the white house -- should I point?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure, if you do not mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. That was your first opportunity to see Omarska camp other than the times you had been going through the cordon of guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you see as you sat there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw, in fact, I saw a real confusion. Some people were running towards the dining room and the other ones were running towards them in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see any other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the bottom of the green part there, the guards with large fire hoses were bathing the prisoners, the inmates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were these prisoners clothed? Were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: They were naked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were naked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You said they were "bathing" the prisoners -- at least the translation was "they were bathing the prisoners with large fire hoses" -- what was happening as the fire hoses were being directed at these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, some were falling down because of the force of the water from the hoses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Away from the white house where the green part was and where the bushes were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you can just show us where it is? That would be easier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model] It was around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Icic, did you later learn that a relative or a friend had seen you sitting in front of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they then organise an action to get you out of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To do so, was it necessary to bribe a Serb official in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you learn how much money was demanded for your release?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How much was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In fact, I ended up coming out for 100 Swiss francs, but because several of my friends were involved in this, some were asked for 100 deutschemarks, some for 200 and a Serb actually was asking for 200 deutschemarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your friends were able to raise 100 Swiss francs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 100 Swiss francs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did that prove enough to get you moved from the white house to another part of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you moved to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was transferred to the large red building in the last small room called the electric workshop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain there until you were transferred to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Icic, if I could clarify a number of matters with you? When you left Keraterm and arrived at Omarska, the first building that you were held in, was that the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the white house for overall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed the whole time, from with the arrival to Omarska until the day when they bought me -- my fellow inmates bought me for those 100 Swiss francs back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell me how many days that was, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly how many days. But I arrived approximately either on 7th or 8th and I left, I came out on 13th or 14th. That is what I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. You were part of a group of prisoners that had been transferred from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was this group of prisoners from Keraterm made up of, who were you? You told us you were Muslims and Croats, but what was the background of this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people were for the most part from the Ljubija mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The number of people from the Ljubija mine, can you tell me that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were -- almost all of them were from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had not worked at the Ljubija mine. Do you know ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- why you were included in that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know -- to date, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you were then transferred into that white house. If I could just consider the layout of the interior of that house with you? As you go through the door, there are two rooms on the right and two rooms on the left, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the end of the hallway there is an area which is an unfinished wash room or shower area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was simply a small room, smaller than the other ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That room had no tiles on the floor, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no time to look around to see if it had tiles or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you arrived in the white house, as you went through the door you were put in the second room on the right, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know at that time as to whether there were other people inside the white house with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment, no, because I was -- I, in fact, ran into the white house between the guards that were beating me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After you had arrived, how soon was it before you were taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until we were all in the room and we were followed by a man who started calling us out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From what you say it seems then that you were amongst the first to be questioned from that group who arrived from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what time of day it was that you arrived at the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I arrived at the white house around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You went for your questioning, do you know what time that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately after -- when we were all off the bus, there was a short break and we had to go to the interrogations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You went accompanied by a guard to an interrogation in another building, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I went to the interrogation I followed the guard who would not allow me to walk fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long did your interrogation take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But before this interrogation took place, you had been beaten on two occasions, when you arrived at the white house and also ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- when you left the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you been beaten in the room of the white house as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the white house I was not beaten until after the interrogation and I was not beaten even after the interrogation, and the only times that anything happened was when they walked over us or stepped over us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you returned from your interrogation you were then put in another room and am I right in saying, from what you describe, as you enter the white house it is the second room on the left, so at the end of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there other prisoners already in that room when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were only the ones who arrived that day, together with me from Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, when you were put in that new room in the white house, how many people were in that room at that stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment when I arrived from the interrogation there was only myself and two more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As you moved through the white house at this time, were you able to tell how many other people were in the building itself? You knew of the people who were in the first room you were put in, but what about the other two rooms at the front of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not looking. I had no time to look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, a guard was leading me, was taking me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The very small room at the end of the hallway in the white house, can you recollect if people were in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was empty, the one at the end of the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You referred to a lady who was also within the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us where she was placed in the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She told us that she was in the first room to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say "the first room to the right", that is as you enter the front door, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having been put in that second room on the left, did others come and join you in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all of the ones who were interrogated that day joined me in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many people came into that room by the night time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost all of us came there. A few of them were left. They were not interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So that is somewhere between 40 to 50 people, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 40 people, 40, 45, somewhere there. I do not know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had they, some of them, come in in a state of bad physical condition having been beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment we were still not in a bad physical shape. Those were the blows in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Others seemed to have received similar treatment to you, the beating when they arrived and the beating when they left to go to their interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More or less almost all fared the same, perhaps a blow more or less, but pretty much everybody the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The condition of this building at this time, would it be right to say that it was in extremely poor condition because of the stench ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- and what it had been used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not actually know what it was used for, but I remember it by -- according to me, on that day it seemed as if those two rooms were prepared especially for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Some 40 of you in that second room on the left at the back of the building was, presumably, a very cramped space to put that number of people within?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was cramped. We were one on top of each other, like sardines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, this is not a big building and these are not big rooms that we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were paying no attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. When the night time came had you had any opportunity for food that day in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in the white house I never ate anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when you were in the white house you were not given an opportunity to go to the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not leaving the white house until the day when they took us in front of the white house in order for it to be cleaned. I had not left the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By this time you had spent a month and a half in these detention camps, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean Keraterm and Omarska, both?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You knew the kind of regime that you were under?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was a regime where you were kept in fear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a regime of terror.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was a regime where it was dangerous for you to disobey orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was dangerous. If an order is given out, you had to obey it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A danger for you to know too much -- to know the guards, for instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was dangerous for everyone, not just me, anybody who was in Omarska or Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This was a place where you could not look about and be curious to see what was happening around you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on the position you are in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because if one of the guards caught you being curious, you were in immediate risk of being injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended on the guard too. There were those who really, who were enjoying for you to see him before he starts torturing you. They seemed to have been taking pleasure from torturing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know at this time that Krkan's shift was a shift that was regarded by people in Omarska as being the worst shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was in Omarska, I found out only when I left the white house, I heard that Krkan's was one of the worst shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The rooms that you were in in the white house had doors, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These rooms where I was had only openings, whereas the doors had been taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there not doors that were closed on the rooms so that you were kept in the rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was in these two rooms there were no doors, that is, door panes were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you include within that the room that was the second room on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second one to the right and the second to the left, it was either whoever was in one of those two places could see from one room to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Icic, I would like you to look at this photograph and perhaps if we can have called up on the screen 22-22? It is Exhibit 240 produced earlier by the Prosecution. I do not know if we are able to get 22-22? I do not think the technicians are able to do it, so perhaps if that photograph can be placed on the overhead projector so that the Court can see it?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What Exhibit is that, number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit 240, your Honour. Mr. Bos has another here. So if Mr. Bos could put that on the monitor? Thank you. This is a photograph, Mr. Icic, taken in the white house from the room which is the second room on the right as you enter. You can see on that photograph that there is a door with an enclosed panel at the bottom, glass above. This door is affixed to that room where you were first placed. You can see across the corridor what would be the first room on the left and there is also a door to that room. What I put to you is this, that there were doors on those rooms in the white house. What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, nothing. They might have put them later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They were not there then when you were in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because what I also suggest to you is that, in fact, these doors were shut whilst you were in your rooms in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This door was never shut to those two rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. What I want to talk to you now about is what happened after you were beaten in the room and your clothing slashed and Krkan had attempted to extort money from you. After that had happened, you say that men entered the white house with lighting and other equipment. What do you mean by that, what sort of lighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they did not come in with lighting. They came in with gear, with equipment for lighting, so as to set up lighting in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why was lighting being put in the hallway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They must have known that. I did not know it, why did they put the lighting in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because this was night time and it was dark, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was no electric light within your rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So far as you could tell, the other rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In other rooms, neither in the room across there was no light either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The room where you went to be questioned, if you could identify that room again to us, which room it was as you entered the white house through the front door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no interrogation rooms in the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You described, though, going into a room where others had been and where beatings took place upon you as an individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was -- I described that from the bus together with my colleagues, those who had arrived with me, got to the last room on the right, but that was not the interrogation room. The interrogation room is in a completely different building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, but you describe during the night time being taken to another room having been called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I was called out, but that was not the interrogation room. That was the beating room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could then identify to us as you walked through the front door which room you would call the "beating room"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, as you enter the white house it was the room at the end of the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the left or right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the small room at the end of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was that small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That room was a very small room indeed, not much bigger than a shower cubicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would not say a shower cubicle. A shower cubicle is very small. Since I work in construction, I know how large a shower booth can be, 60 by 80, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, but the room where you say you were called into and beaten by five or six men, are you saying that that is the room at the end of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that is the room at the end of the corridor where we were taken in one by one that evening and beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So what was the lighting used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, presumably, so that they could see. Those who beat us, so that they could see what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This room would have been a room that was with a screen from the hallway, so that you had to go through a doorway to get into it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had nothing, no screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it just an open area at the end of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was simply like these other rooms, it also would have doors, but it did not have a door. There was no panel or, at least, I did not notice it. At any rate, there was no obstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were beaten in this area, how many people were in that area with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I entered that room, there was nobody else but those who beat me and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So how many people would that put in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, five of them and myself as the sixth one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How exactly were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I did not see. I had no time to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You described having a noose around your neck and you fell to the floor. This was a way of holding you or restraining you with the rope around your neck, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one of them was holding me with a noose which was very tight, and I was struggling for air and the rest I could not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long after that beating that took place in the room when your clothing had been slashed with knives did this take place? How long after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the slashing of clothes did not happen after this event. It was before. It was while there was still daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I know that and that was, in fact, my question. What I wanted to know was the gap between the two incidents that took place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I could not tell you. One of the incidents took place in day time and the other one at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The earlier incident involving the slashing of the clothing concerned Krkan's guards and his shift, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see those people, whose shift it was, and who were those people, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But Krkan seemed to have been involved because he was the one who was asking you to write down your names and what money or valuables you had on the sheet of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was always the one calling out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This group that attacked you in this room included someone called Duca, is that right, or Duca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Also known by you as Dule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never knew him as Dule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am 100 per cent, I never even knew that he was Dule. I knew that that was Duca from Orlovci, but he could -- he could have also been Dule. It was possible because Serbs used it as an abbreviation, Dule, Dusko. I mean, all those could be one and the same name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you not referred to him in a statement written by you in your own hand as "Dule, known as Duca"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, maybe when I was writing that it is a slip of the hand but, to my mind, it is all the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I am interested about is why you should be so concerned to say that that is a slip of the hand and not something you would have used as an expression?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, normal expression for a man is if you know his full name, if you were friends with him, if you socialised with him, but I never did, neither were we friends, nor we socialised. I met him as a bad man in Keraterm who came daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But are you trying to conceal from us the fact that Duca was called by you "Dule" because of this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because what I will do is I will show you this statement written by you in your own hand on 12th February 1993 where you refer to that. This will be D28, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: D27. [To the witness]: Do you remember writing this in February 1993, Mr. Icic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
